To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the density of GABAA receptor binding sites increases with postnatal development in rat brain, while the affinity of the binding sites remains relatively constant.

1) the density of GABAbinding sites in rat forebrain is low in the neonate and increases rapidly during the first 2 weeks postnatal, 2) the affinity of GABAbindingsites is similar in the neonate as it is in the adult, 3) freeze-thawing and detergent extraction of rat brain membranes causes increases in the affinity for GABA, and 4) there is a greater increase in the affinity of the GABA binding sites
the density of GABAB receptors in the forebrain increases with age and that the endogenous inhibitors of the GABAB receptors increase with age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the development of the inhibitory transmitter GABA.
the postnatal development of GABAB binding sites in the rat forebrain and the effects of freeze-thawing and Triton extraction of these membranes.
the development of the inhibitory neurotransmission system in the mammalian brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the density of GABAB receptors is low at birth but increases rapidly during the first postnatal week.

the development of GABAergic neurotransmission in the rat brain is a complex process which involves the development of GABAA receptor binding sites, the endogenous inhibitors of those binding sites and, perhaps most importantly, the development of the endogenous inhibitors themselves.
there are no changes in the affinity of the binding sites, but there are increases in their density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the GABA binding sites in neonatal rat are more sensitive to endogenous inhibitors than those in adult rat brain, and that there is a developmental increase in both the number of GABA binding site and the number of endogenous inhibitors.
there is an increase in the density of GABAB receptors in neonatal rat forebrain and a concomitant increase in the density and affinity of GABAA receptors in the cerebellum.

GABA binding sites in neonatal rat forebrain and in cerebellum are subject to inhibition by endogenous factors which are removed by freeze-thawing and detergent extraction of the membrane preparations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GABA receptors in the developing brain may be more sensitive to inhibition by endogenous substances than in the mature brain.
the development of GABAergic synapses and GABAergic neurotransmission is a very complex process, and that there are a lot of different factors that are involved.
the development of GABAergic inhibition in the brain may be related to decreases in endogenous inhibitors of binding sites for this neurotransmitter.
